title: TF primitive parameterization field guide for VPC/IAM/EKS
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a practical field guide for designing Terraform primitives that back private deployments (VPC, IAM, and Kubernetes primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS). The goal is a small, composable set of primitives with stable input/output contracts and a clear upgrade/migration story. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: conventions, variable shapes, output shapes, compatibility rules, and an upgrade runbook for module authors and integrators.

High level design principles (summary):
- Minimal, opinionated surface area: prefer explicit inputs over magic; keep the module focused on a single responsibility.
- Stable contracts: inputs and outputs are the public API. Breakages require major-version bumps and migration guides.
- Validation over silence: validate required formats (CIDR, region, list lengths) proactively in Terraform using validation blocks.
- Backwards-friendly defaults: do not add new required inputs in minor releases; provide automatic mapping where possible.
- Semantic versioning for modules: follow semver strictly (patch = bugfix, minor = additive/backwards compatible features, major = breaking changes).

Conventions for variable parameterization:
- Naming: use snake_case with clear nouns: vpc_cidr, private_subnets_cidrs, public_subnets_cidrs, service_account_annotations.
- Types: prefer constrained types where possible: list(object({ name = string, cidr = string })), map(string) for tags.
- Descriptions: every variable must have a descriptive "description" explaining expected shape and constraints.
- Defaults: Provide sensible defaults that reflect typical enterprise policy but allow explicit override. No default should cause resource creation in a different account or region.
- Sensitive: mark values that may contain secrets as sensitive = true (e.g., kms_key_arn if customer-managed).

Examples: VPC primitive inputs (recommended shape):
- variable "vpc_name" { type = string description = "Logical name used in tags and resource names" }
- variable "vpc_cidr" { type = string description = "Primary VPC CIDR (must be /16 -/22)" validation { condition = can(regex("^\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+\\/\\d+$", var.vpc_cidr)) error_message = "vpc_cidr must be a valid CIDR" } }
- variable "subnets" { type = list(object({ name = string, cidr = string, az = optional(string) })) description = "List of subnets with name and cidr. Ordering is used to map to AZs when az omitted." }
- variable "tags" { type = map(string) default = {} description = "Tags applied to VPC and children resources" }

VPC outputs (recommended shape):
- output "vpc_id" { value = aws_vpc.main.id description = "ID of the created VPC" }
- output "subnets" { value = [for s in aws_subnet.private : { name = s.tags.Name, id = s.id, cidr = s.cidr_block }] description = "List of subnets (name, id, cidr)" }
- output "route_table_ids" { value = aws_route_table.rts[*].id }

IAM primitive notes (service accounts and role contracts):
- Principle: keep roles minimal and parameterized by permissionset (e.g., eks_node_role, app_runtime_role).
- Inputs: assume_role_policy_doc, managed_policy_arns (list), inline_policy (string map by name), trust_principals (list).
- Outputs should include role_arn, role_id, role_name. Provide an output map for policy attachment ARNs for downstream auditing.
- Avoid embedding environment-specific logic (e.g., team names) in role names; instead expose a name_prefix input to be provided by the caller.

Kubernetes cluster primitives (EKS/GKE/AKS) - cross-cloud considerations:
- Keep cluster creation minimal: cluster control plane resources and a node_group primitive. Do not mix networking creation into the cluster primitive if a VPC primitive is used by the same consumer.
- Inputs: cluster_name, kubernetes_version, vpc_id (optional for managed vpc), subnet_ids (list), oidc_provider_enabled (bool), node_pools (list(object({ name = string, instance_type = string, desired_count = number, autoscaling = optional(object(...)) }))).
- Outputs: cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca, kubeconfig (sensitive), node_pool_ids, oidc_provider_arn.
- Provider differences: document small differences:
  - EKS: requires subnet tagging (kubernetes.io/cluster/<name>=shared) for the AWS Cloud Provider and may need additional IAM roles for OIDC-based IRSA.
  - GKE: network mode may be auto or custom; if custom, subnets are regional. GKE provides private cluster options that change master_auth flows.
  - AKS: consider managed identity vs service principal; node pools are resource "azurerm_kubernetes_cluster_node_pool" and SKU compatibility matters.

Outputs shaping and consumer ergonomics:
- Provide both typed outputs and convenient flattened maps for common lookups: e.g., subnets_by_role = { private = [ids], public = [ids] } and subnets_detailed = [{ name, id, cidr }].
- Avoid leaking provider-specific ARNs unless necessary; if provided, prefix outputs (aws_vpc_arn, gke_network_self_link) so downstream modules can pick what they need.

Versioning and upgrade rules:
- No breaking changes in patch/minor releases. Breaking changes = removing or renaming inputs/outputs, changing types, or changing the resource lifecycle semantics.
- For a breaking change: create a migration branch and a compatibility shim that supports old names mapping to new inputs for at least one minor release, plus an automated deprecation warning via plan-time null_resource with terraform local-exec echo (best-effort).
- Use a CHANGELOG.md for each module with clear upgrade steps and an example plan/apply command sequence.

Upgrade runbook (consumer-facing) - recommended steps for module consumers when module major version increments:
1) Read CHANGELOG and migration guide (link to module release).
2) Update module source reference in consumer tf code to new semver tag.
3) Run terraform init -upgrade.
4) Run terraform plan -out=tfplan -input=false. Inspect for resource replacements and attribute renames.
5) If outputs changed name, add a shim in consumer code mapping old_output = try(module.new_mod.new_output, module.old_mod.old_output) where possible; otherwise plan a two-phase deploy: first lift outputs into state-only resources (terraform state mv) then replace.
6) Roll out in staging and monitor for drift/permission errors.
7) After stable, apply in prod.

Migration pattern examples (non-breaking shim):
- New input vpc_subnets -> old input public_subnets + private_subnets: accept both shapes, prefer new if provided, and include validation that the combination is not ambiguous. Explicitly log a deprecation warning in module outputs or via a data.null_resource hack.

Testing and CI expectations:
- Unit/plan tests: use terratest or terraform-provider-tester to assert plan contains expected resources for a matrix of inputs (minimal, default, specialized).
- Integration: short-lived real account integration runs in an ephemeral account (or dedicated test account) that creates/destroys resources. Keep durations minimal, and use tagging to clean up orphaned resources.
- Upgrade regression tests: maintain a test that runs terraform init/plan against the previous stable tag vs the candidate tag and detects changes to outputs or resource replacements.

Operational considerations for on-prem and VPC edge cases:
- IPAM: expect consumers to supply subnets for on-prem clusters. Avoid auto-allocation heuristics that assume cloud IPAM.
- CNI: expose a cni_plugin input (calico/amazon-vpc-cni/cilium) and avoid hard-wiring policy. Document recommended defaults for throughput/scale.
- BGP/metal LB: provide hooks for externalLB config (external_lb_address, bgp_neighbors) rather than prescribing implementation.

Checklist for module authors before releasing a new minor/major version:
- [ ] Variable and output definitions included and documented in README.md
- [ ] Validation blocks where possible for formats and constraints
- [ ] Default tags and name_prefix behavior documented
- [ ] Upgrade/migration guide written with plan/apply examples
- [ ] Unit and integration tests added to CI matrix
- [ ] CHANGELOG updated with explicit migration steps
- [ ] Deprecation shims for renamed inputs/outputs added for one minor cycle (if possible)

Open questions and where to get alignment:
- How long should we support deprecation shims? (proposal: one minor version)
- Standardize a small set of tag keys and name_prefix behavior across all primitives (proposal: team, env, project, managed_by)
- Decide on a canonical shape for kubeconfig outputs (sensitive string vs file).

Appendix: small recommended variable & output list (copy/paste friendly)
- variable "name_prefix" { type = string description = "short prefix for resources (team or project)" default = "rdw" }
- variable "environment" { type = string description = "env tag (dev/stg/prod)" default = "dev" }
- output "ids" { value = { vpc = aws_vpc.main.id, subnets = aws_subnet.private[*].id } description = "quick id map" }

Notes to reviewers: this is a working playbook draft. I'm expecting feedback on the recommended deprecation period, the exact shapes for subnet objects, and anything missing for the on-prem/metal path. If we like the direction we can turn this into a templated README generator for modules to include with each PR.

Last edited by: Avery Collins (engineering - private deployments) on 2025-01-15
